newsitem.title: KENYA: Stone-throwing students take to Nairobi streets.
newsitem.headline: Stone-throwing students take to Nairobi streets.

text.p: Stone-throwing students took to the streets of Nairobi on Monday and clashed with riot police, a week after the worst political unrest in Kenya in seven years, witnesses said.

Reuters correspondents at the scene said thousands of Kenya Polytechnic students had seized control of Haile Selassie Avenue, a major road through the city centre, throwing stones and demanding constitutional reforms before a general election.
They said dozens of riot and crack General Service Unit police had arrived and were firing tear gas and advancing in a bid to drive the students back into the polytechnic campus.

There were no immediate reports of casualties in the unrest in the Kenyan capital on Monday, a week after nine people were killed during unrest in Nairobi and other towns and cities and fierce clashes between demonstrators and riot police.

Opposition-backed groups demand constitutional reforms before presidential and parliamentary elections this year. No date has been set for the polls but President Daniel arap Moi has said there is too little time for them before the election.
